title: 12 Indian Vegan Meals for $18: Breakfasts, Lunch, and Dinner (Meal Prep)
summary: Goodful’s video presents Kanchan, founder of Spice Spice Baby, demonstrating how to prepare 12 Indian vegan meals for about $18. The session blends nutrition-focused tips with practical cooking steps: two breakfast oat blends (one with chia, oats, cinnamon, cardamom and berries; a second golden-milk version with heated turmeric and fat to activate curcumin, topped with kiwi and mango), a lunch of aloo tikki with a lentil salad plus two sauces (vegan yogurt sauce and cilantro-mint chutney), and a dairy-free dinner featuring a tofu-based saag paneer-inspired dish and a sumac-dusted chana masala, with serving variations like naan or Israeli couscous. Techniques highlighted include binding patties with sandwich bread, pan-searing for texture, making a batch onion-ginger-garlic paste, pressing tofu to mimic paneer, blending chutneys, and finishing dishes with sumac and spices. Throughout, nutritional notes touch on omega-3s from chia, the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties of turmeric and kiwis, and the concept of resistant starch in cooled potatoes.

sections.title: Breakfast prep: Overnight oats and turmeric golden milk
sections.description: Two overnight oats batches are prepared. The first uses plant-based milk with chia seeds and rolled oats, flavored with cinnamon and cardamom and sweetened with maple syrup, topped with berries. The second batch uses golden milk (heated plant-based milk with turmeric) to activate curcumin, plus chia, oats, and maple, finished with chopped kiwi and mango for a tropical twist. The host notes the gut-health and antioxidant benefits of chia, oats, and berries, and explains turmeric’s bioactive compounds require heat and fat to be most effective.

sections.title: Lunch: Aloo tikki with lentil salad and chutneys
concepts: lentil salad with cucumber and carrots
sections.description: Lunch centers on aloo tikki patties bound with sandwich bread, pan-seared until golden. A simple vegan yogurt sauce and a cilantro-mint chutney (blended with shallots, ginger, garlic, lime, salt, sugar) are prepared for variety. A quick lentil salad with cooked lentils, cucumber, carrots, lime juice, cilantro, and chaat masala provides fiber and phytonutrients. The dish emphasizes texture, brightness from lime and chutney, and a note on resistant starch when using cooled potatoes.

sections.title: Dinner: Saag-paneer-style tofu with sumac chana masala
concepts: roasted spices in a tomato base
spinach and frozen spinach for nutrition
naan or Israeli couscous as serving options
sections.description: Dinner features a dairy-free saag paneer-inspired dish using pressed and pan-seared extra-firm tofu to imitate paneer. The sauce starts with cumin seeds and an onion-ginger-garlic paste, then tomato and spices are roasted before adding pureed spinach. The tofu is simmered in the spiced sauce, and the dish is plated with either naan or Israeli couscous for variety. A separate sumac-dusted chana masala (with chickpeas and spinach) is finished with bay leaf and spinach, highlighting antioxidant and anti-inflammatory notes. The segment also reinforces a batch-prep approach for aromatics and suggests grain variation to diversify texture and nutrition.
